## Body

PASS-WITH-NOTES — performance/282, round 1, exact head db3ae4d29c932a8629499e564e1aa745156c9b28.

No blocking performance finding. Exact HEAD and the nine-file fdd6ad1e..db3ae4d delta inspected. One retained release benchmark replayed at niceness 19; no rebuild, deployment, daemon change or live fleet measurement.

Benchmark: 2,000,000 iterations/path, three rounds; one ignored test passed in 0.27 s. Replay added 39.9 / 39.8 / 40.3 ns/request, consistent with the author's 40.9-42.1 ns. Provenance: retained pre-rebase benchmark binary, base 9ffc5729 plus the F231 implementation, not a new final-head build. Source and original receipts inspected. It measures a warm, successful, ready, held_us=0 path: outer clocks, one Tokio scope poll, split and Outcomes::record. Unchanged route lookup/method selection, HeldSpan and held_us atomic are excluded.

[INFERENCE] At 12-17 responses/s that READY-PATH component is 0.478-0.685 microseconds CPU/s (0.0000478-0.0000685% of one core). This is not the complete fleet overhead. Tokio 1.53.1 stores the scope inline, with thread-local RefCell swap/restore on each poll/drop: no added Box or mutex. Pending polls/cancellations cost extra; each HeldSpan adds two clock reads and a saturating task-local Cell update; held completions add another relaxed atomic. The ledger's request-rate-only cost statement needs this qualification.

Existing wait-hook rates, absent external wakeups: native idle 2 spans/s/pending claim (during-turn backstop 1/15 s), dispatch 40/s/waiter, spawn registration 20/s/waiter, footer and dead-pane waits 4/s/waiter. Notifications can add inbox wakeups. These rates describe existing waits, not new timers. Span/poll overhead was not separately benchmarked. No new loop, timer, launch or hot-path lock; existing outcome/query counts remain, timing adds one or two relaxed atomics. Counter storage grows 128 bytes/template plus 16 unmatched bytes, independent of seats or request history; snapshot adds two loads/slot and two numeric fields/requested route.

What it enables after deployment: take paired ping/CPU TIME/spawn readings over a known window at the SAME PID, commit and process-start identity. Per route compute completed count delta, requests/s and delta_active_us/delta_count (mean non-park wall latency); rank delta_active_us/(1e6*elapsed_s) to find high non-park handler occupancy. Inspect held separately and use sufficiently long windows for long-poll completions. Counters update on completion, are nontransactional and wrap: they do not measure arrivals or in-flight work.

active_us is NOT CPU time: SQLx queue/I/O awaits, lock waits and scheduler delay remain active. A cheap route waiting behind another route's SQL can look expensive; detached/background work is not assigned by this layer. Use rankings to select candidates, then require CPU TIME plus stack/rate agreement or an owner-approved controlled workload comparison before naming a culprit. These counters alone cannot explain the historical 22.5%, or establish causality against the later 17.5% window. F231/F222 diagnosis stays OPEN.

References: http/route_counts.rs:79-138,198-260,303-332; the five added lexical wait spans; docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:97-111; locked Tokio task_local.rs scope/poll implementation. Correctness/security verdicts remain with their holders.
